title: He Was Chosen by God... Yet He Hid Among the Baggage
paragraphs:
He Was Chosen by God... Yet He Hid Among the Baggage
The Day Saul Ran From the Crown—and the Warning Every Believer Must Hear Before They Miss Their Calling
There is a moment in Scripture that feels almost unbelievable.
Israel was about to receive its very first king.
He had already been chosen by God.
Yet when the moment finally arrived...
while God's chosen leader was nowhere to be seen.
The scene almost feels tragic enough to make you stop reading.
many of us have hidden in exactly the same place.
And perhaps that's why Saul's story continues to expose hearts thousands of years later.
Because many people ask God to reveal His purpose...
The Bible records the moment with striking simplicity.
"Therefore they inquired again of the LORD, 'Is there still a man to come?' And the LORD said, 'Behold, he has hidden himself among the baggage.'" (1 Samuel 10:22, ESV)
The Hebrew text says Saul had hidden among the כֵּלִים (kēlîm).
The word kēlîm literally means articles, vessels, equipment, baggage, possessions, containers, or implements.
Everything that distracted from the calling God had placed upon him.
The future king was surrounded by things...
instead of standing where God had called him.
Insecurity whispers, "Stay where nobody expects anything."
The tragedy isn't simply that Saul hid.
The tragedy is that God already knew exactly where he was.
"Where shall I go from your Spirit? Or where shall I flee from your presence?" (Psalm 139:7)
No hiding place is invisible to Heaven.
Yet Saul's fear did not begin that day.
Earlier, after Samuel privately anointed him with oil, Scripture says,
"Then Samuel took the flask of oil and poured it on his head and kissed him and said, 'Has not the LORD anointed you to be prince over his people Israel?'" (1 Samuel 10:1)
The Hebrew word translated "anointed" comes from מָשַׁח (māšaḥ).
It means to smear, consecrate, dedicate, set apart for God's purpose.
This wasn't merely a symbolic ceremony.
Yet being chosen by God never automatically removes human fear.
Many believers assume courage arrives before obedience.
The greatest obstacle was never Saul's lack of gifting.
The greatest obstacle was Saul himself.
His heart wrestled with something many Christians secretly battle.
Earlier he had even answered Samuel,
"Am I not a Benjaminite... from the least of the tribes...?" (1 Samuel 9:21)
But false humility often disguises unbelief.
False humility keeps staring at our inability.
but his heart never fully left the baggage.
That hidden fear slowly grew roots.
It was lost little by little.
Every compromise watered the seeds planted inside the baggage.
This makes the story far more sobering.
The hiding wasn't merely one embarrassing moment.
It revealed a heart that never completely surrendered.
The Hebrew Scriptures consistently connect the heart with the word לֵב (lēv).
The lēv is not merely emotion.
It is the center of thought.
God was never simply looking for a king with stature.
He was searching for a surrendered heart.
Later, when David would be chosen, Scripture famously declares,
"Man looks on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart." (1 Samuel 16:7)
Everything changed because of the condition of the lēv.
Even in the New Testament the same principle remains.
Jesus repeatedly confronted outward religion while exposing inward hearts.
When Jesus calls His followers, He never promises comfort.
The Greek verb ἀκολουθέω (akoloutheō) literally means to accompany, to walk behind, to continue following as a disciple.
Discipleship has never been about self-confidence.
It has always been about Christ-confidence.
Perhaps that's exactly where someone reading this finds themselves today.
Yet fear has convinced you that hiding feels safer.
Just as He knew exactly where Saul was.
The beautiful news of the Gospel is this:
Jesus never calls us because we are already sufficient.
He calls us because He is.
"But God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise... so that no human being might boast in the presence of God." (1 Corinthians 1:27–29)
The Kingdom has always advanced through surrendered people, not impressive people.
This is where Saul's story points us beyond Saul.
Where Saul hid from his calling...
Jesus set His face toward Jerusalem.
Where Saul lost a kingdom through disobedience...
Jesus established an eternal Kingdom through perfect obedience.
"Not my will, but yours, be done." (Luke 22:42)
That single prayer reversed what humanity had broken since Eden.
The cross is where every fearful heart finds hope.
The empty tomb is where every failed beginning finds a new ending.
That is why our message has always been...
Maybe you've spent years hiding among your own baggage.
His grace reaches farther than your hiding place.
His mercy is deeper than your shame.
His cross is stronger than your past.
His resurrection is greater than your fear.
And if Christ has truly become your King, then let your life point others to Him. If you desire to glorify God through the faithful spread of His Word, your support becomes part of that mission.
If this story reminded you that God is still calling your name, don't keep it to yourself.

What baggage has been hardest for you to leave behind? If this message spoke to your heart, comment, "Christ is still healing me," or "No more hiding," as a testimony that your confidence is no longer in yourself but in Jesus Christ.
Because someday every believer will stand before the true King.
none of the baggage we carried will matter.
Only whether we followed the One who carried our cross before we ever carried our own.
